title: Review 4
description: Demonstratives, accusative case, prepositional case, and prepositions
descriptionRussian: Указательные местоимения, винительный падеж, предложный падеж и предлоги
intro: This review covers demonstrative pronouns (этот/тот), the accusative case for direct objects, the prepositional case for locations, and key prepositions like в and на. These topics work together: 'I see this house' uses accusative, while 'I live in this house' uses prepositional — same noun, different cases depending on the role in the sentence.
rules: Demonstrative pronouns agree with the noun: этот дом (m), эта книга (f), это окно (n), эти люди (pl). Тот/та/то/те = 'that'.
Accusative case marks the direct object. Masculine animate and feminine nouns change: маму (f -а→-у), брата (m animate +а). Masculine inanimate and neuter don't change.
Prepositional case is used after в (in) and на (on/at) for location: в доме, на столе, в школе.
В + prepositional = inside: в магазине (in the store). На + prepositional = on/at: на работе (at work).
Prepositional endings: masculine/neuter -е (доме, окне), feminine -е (школе), some nouns use -и (площади).
examples: Я вижу этот дом. (I see this house.) — accusative, m. inanimate = no change
Я вижу эту книгу. (I see this book.) — accusative feminine: эта → эту, книга → книгу
Мы живём в этом доме. (We live in this house.) — prepositional after в
Книга на столе. (The book is on the table.) — prepositional after на

items.explanation: Эта changes to эту in the accusative case for feminine nouns.
Этот is the masculine nominative form of the demonstrative pronoun.
Книга is feminine. In accusative case, -а changes to -у: книгу.

items.hint: Masculine animate nouns change in accusative
items.explanation: Брат is masculine animate. Animate masculine nouns add -а in accusative: брата.
В + prepositional case means 'in/inside'. Мы живём в Москве.

items.promptEnglish: The book is lying on the table.
items.explanation: На + prepositional case means 'on'. Книга на столе = The book is on the table.
After в (location), use prepositional case. Школа → школе.

items.prompt: Я вижу _____ стол. (this, masculine accusative inanimate)
items.explanation: For masculine inanimate nouns, accusative = nominative. Этот стол stays этот стол.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Accusative and prepositional case forms with demonstratives and possessives

minimalPairs.explanation: Masculine inanimate nouns don't change in accusative. Стол stays стол.
Masculine animate nouns change in accusative: брат → брата.
В + prepositional is used for 'in/inside' a building. На is used for 'at/on' surfaces or certain fixed expressions.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The book is on the table.
minimalPairs.explanation: На + prepositional means 'on' a surface. В means 'in/inside'.

sentenceBuilding.translation: We live in a big house.
The cat is sitting on the table.

reviewVocab.example: Я живу в Москве. (Москве — предложный падеж)
Этот дом, эта книга, это окно, эти люди.
